prop:finite-graph-count.proof_tex:
Let \(H=G[I_R]\).  A directed graph on three labelled response vertices is determined by a subset of the six possible off-diagonal arrows.  Count acyclic choices by the number \(m\) of edges in the underlying undirected skeleton.  For \(m=0,1,2,3\), respectively, the numbers of labelled acyclic orientations are
\[
1,\qquad {3\choose1}2=6,\qquad {3\choose2}2^2=12,\qquad 2^3-2=6.
\]
For \(m=2\) the skeleton is a forest, so every orientation is acyclic; for \(m=3\) exactly the two directed three-cycles are excluded.  Hence there are
\[
1+6+12+6=25
\]
possible response DAGs.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}allowed\text{-}edges}\) permits each of the nine arrows \(X_j\to R_i\) independently, and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}graph\text{-}class}\) imposes no further condition on them.  Therefore
\[
|\mathfrak G_3|=25\,2^9=12800.
\]

Now forbid the three self-censoring arrows.  For each response DAG there are \(2^6\) choices of the six remaining substantive-to-response arrows, so the resulting set \(\mathcal A\) has cardinality \(25\,2^6=1600\).  For completeness, the orbit-count identity used below follows by double counting
\[
\mathcal T=\{(\sigma,A)\in\mathfrak S_3\times\mathcal A:\sigma A=A\}.
\]
Counting first by \(\sigma\) gives \(|\mathcal T|=\sum_\sigma|\operatorname{Fix}(\sigma)|\).  For an orbit \(\mathcal O\) and any representative \(A_0\in\mathcal O\), the number of elements carrying \(A_0\) to a fixed \(A\in\mathcal O\) equals \(|\operatorname{Stab}(A_0)|\), while \(|\mathcal O|\,|\operatorname{Stab}(A_0)|=6\) by the explicit partition of \(\mathfrak S_3\) into those fibres.  Thus every orbit contributes exactly six pairs to \(\mathcal T\), and
\[
|\mathcal A/\mathfrak S_3|=\frac16\sum_{\sigma\in\mathfrak S_3}|\operatorname{Fix}(\sigma)|.
\]
The identity fixes all \(1600\) elements.  Fix a transposition, say \((12)\).  On the six response arrows, the orbit \(\{R_1\to R_2,R_2\to R_1\}\) must be absent in an invariant DAG, while the other two arrow orbits may be chosen as neither, both arrows into \(R_3\), or both arrows out of \(R_3\).  Thus precisely three response DAGs are fixed.  The six non-self substantive arrows form three two-element orbits, giving \(2^3=8\) invariant masks.  Hence every transposition fixes \(3\cdot8=24\) elements of \(\mathcal A\).  Under a three-cycle, the six response arrows form the two directed three-cycle orbits; acyclicity forces both absent.  The six substantive arrows form two orbits, so a three-cycle fixes \(2^2=4\) elements.  The double-count identity now gives
\[
|\mathcal A/\mathfrak S_3|
=\frac{1600+3\cdot24+2\cdot4}{6}
=280.
\]
This proves both asserted counts.

snapshot.stmt: \[|\mathfrak G_3|=25\cdot2^9=12800,\qquad |\{G\in\mathfrak G_3:X_i\not\to R_i\text{ for every }i\in I\}/\mathfrak S_3|=280.\]

lem:certificate-denominator-safety.proof_tex:
Fix \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\), \(p\in\mathcal M_+(G)\), and \(q=C_{\#}p\).  For any \(w\in\mathcal W\), define \(r(w)\in\mathcal B\) by \(r_i(w)=1\) when \(w_i\in\{0,1\}\) and \(r_i(w)=0\) when \(w_i=?\).  Choose \(x(w)\in\mathcal B\) with \(x_i(w)=w_i\) on observed coordinates and, for definiteness, \(x_i(w)=0\) on missing coordinates.  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}coarsening\text{-}map}\) gives
\[
C(x(w),r(w))=w.
\]
Thus the fibre in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}law}\) is nonempty.  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}strict\text{-}positivity}\) gives \(p(x(w),r(w))>0\), and hence
\[
q_w=\sum_{(x,r):C(x,r)=w}p(x,r)\ge p(x(w),r(w))>0.
\]
If \(\varnothing\ne A\subseteq\mathcal W\), choosing any \(w_0\in A\) yields
\[
q(A)=\sum_{w\in A}q_w\ge q_{w_0}>0.
\]

By Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}language}\), a quotient in an \(\mathrm{ID}\) term can be formed only with a denominator represented as \(q(A)\) for an explicitly encoded nonempty event \(A\).  Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}checker}\) checks that condition for every input and output divisor of every graph-factorization, conditional-independence, grouped-fixing, intervention-fixing, and odds-ratio constructor.  The inequality just proved therefore applies to every divisor in every checker-accepted \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificate, uniformly over \(p\in\mathcal M_+(G)\).

snapshot.stmt: For every \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\), \(p\in\mathcal M_+(G)\), and \(q=C_{\#}p\), one has \(q_w>0\) for every \(w\in\mathcal W\), and therefore \(q(A)=\sum_{w\in A}q_w>0\) for every nonempty \(A\subseteq\mathcal W\). For each graph-factorization, conditional-independence, grouped-fixing, intervention-fixing, and odds-ratio constructor of \(\mathcal L_3\), every checker-accepted input or output divisor has this form; consequently every divisor in every checker-accepted \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificate is strictly positive throughout \(\mathcal M_+(G)\).

defs.def:certificate-checker: \(\operatorname{Check}_3(G,\gamma)\) parses \(\gamma\in\mathcal L_3\), evaluates every graph and rational identity by exact arithmetic, verifies for every graph-factorization, conditional-independence, grouped-fixing, intervention-fixing, and odds-ratio constructor that each input and output divisor is \(q(A)\) for an explicitly encoded nonempty event \(A\subseteq\mathcal W\), and verifies every \(\mathrm{NONID}\) table entry, factorization, coarsened-cell equality, strict-positivity inequality, and target-cell inequality.
defs.def:certificate-language: \(\mathcal L_3\) has two terminal forms. An \(\mathrm{ID}\) term contains eight expressions formed from the coordinates of \(q\) by finite sums, products, and quotients; every quotient denominator is encoded as \(q(A)=\sum_{w\in A}q_w\) for a checker-certified nonempty event \(A\subseteq\mathcal W\). Its trace uses graph factorization, conditional independence, grouped fixing, intervention fixing, or Chen odds-ratio identities, and each constructor records all input and output divisors. A \(\mathrm{NONID}\) term contains two rational \(64\)-cell tables, their graph-factorized conditional tables, exact equality of their \(27\) coarsened cells, strict-positivity checks, and a named cell where their target marginals differ.

thm:certificate-soundness.proof_tex:
Fix \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\).  First suppose that \(\operatorname{Check}_3\) accepts an \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificate \(\gamma\) with terminal expression \(F_G\).  We prove by induction along the finite trace of \(\gamma\) the invariant that every carried rational expression equals, for every \(p\in\mathcal M_+(G)\), the full-law quantity named by its trace label after substituting \(q=C_{\#}p\).

At an observed-coordinate leaf the invariant is exactly Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}law}\).  It is preserved by finite sums and products by ordinary algebra.  At a quotient node, Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}denominator\text{-}safety}\) shows that the checker-certified denominator \(q(A)\) is nonzero, so division preserves the checked equality.  At a graph-factorization node, the checked identity is an instance of Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}graph\text{-}factorization}\).  At a conditional-independence node, substituting that factorization and summing the variables omitted by the node gives the checked conditional equality; all conditioning-event probabilities are nonzero by the denominator lemma.  At a grouped-fixing, intervention-fixing, or odds-ratio node, Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}checker}\) requires the checker to verify the corresponding rational identity from its already verified inputs and outputs.  Clearing its encoded denominators is legitimate by the denominator lemma, and the resulting exact identity therefore preserves the invariant.  These cases exhaust the grammar in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}language}\).

The eight terminal labels are the eight target marginals.  Hence, for every \(x\in\mathcal B\), the terminal invariant and the definition of \(p_X\) give
\[
F_G(C_{\#}p)(x)=\sum_{r\in\mathcal B}p(x,r)=p_X(x).
\]

Now suppose that \(\operatorname{Check}_3\) accepts a \(\mathrm{NONID}\) certificate \((p^{(0)},p^{(1)},x_0)\).  By Definitions \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}language}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}checker}\), the parser checks normalization of each rational \(64\)-cell probability table, every entry is checked strictly positive, and the displayed conditional tables are checked against Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}graph\text{-}factorization}\) for \(G\).  Therefore \(p^{(0)},p^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_+(G)\).  For each \(w\in\mathcal W\), the checker also verifies the exact rational equality
\[
\sum_{(x,r):C(x,r)=w}p^{(0)}(x,r)
=
\sum_{(x,r):C(x,r)=w}p^{(1)}(x,r),
\]
which is \(C_{\#}p^{(0)}=C_{\#}p^{(1)}\) by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}law}\).  Finally, its named-cell check is precisely
\[
\sum_r p^{(0)}(x_0,r)\ne\sum_r p^{(1)}(x_0,r),
\]
or \(p_X^{(0)}(x_0)\ne p_X^{(1)}(x_0)\).  This proves both soundness assertions.

snapshot.stmt: For every \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\), if \(\operatorname{Check}_3\) accepts an \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificate with functional \(F_G\), then \(F_G(C_{\#}p)=p_X\) for every \(p\in\mathcal M_+(G)\). If it accepts a \(\mathrm{NONID}\) certificate \((p^{(0)},p^{(1)},x_0)\), then \(p^{(0)},p^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_+(G)\), \(C_{\#}p^{(0)}=C_{\#}p^{(1)}\), and \(p_X^{(0)}(x_0)\ne p_X^{(1)}(x_0)\).

thm:certified-reduction.proof_tex:
The exact finite reduction and both nonidentification compilers are established, and the supplied rational-arithmetic program was rerun successfully. There are \(25(2^9-2^6)=11200\) graphs containing a self-censoring arrow. For any such arrow \(X_i\to R_i\), take one law with \(p_X(X_i=1)=1/2\) and \(p(R_i=1\mid X_i=0,1)=(1/2,1/2)\), and a second with \(p_X(X_i=1)=3/5\) and \(p(R_i=1\mid X_i=0,1)=(5/8,5/12)\). Let the remaining two substantive variables and response indicators be independent fair bits. Both coarsened laws have one-item probabilities \((1/4,1/4,1/2)\); hence their \(27\) coarsened cells agree by product factorization. Their minimum \(64\)-cell probabilities are \(1/64\) and \(3/320\), while the target cell with \(X_i=1\) and the other substantive coordinates zero has masses \(1/8\) and \(3/20\). Ignoring additional parents preserves graph factorization, so these rational positive twins cover all \(11200\) graphs.

For a response DAG with \(m\) skeleton edges, inclusion--exclusion gives respectively \(0,16,28,37\) substantive masks containing a criss-cross obstruction for \(m=0,1,2,3\). Since the \(25\) response DAGs have multiplicities \(1,6,12,6\), this yields
\[
6\cdot16+12\cdot28+6\cdot37=654.
\]
For the oriented obstruction \(R_1\to R_2\), \(X_2\to R_1\), \(X_1\to R_2\), the two substantive tables
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1/3&1/6\\1/6&1/3\end{pmatrix},\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}3/10&11/60\\3/20&11/30\end{pmatrix}
\]
are paired, respectively, with
\[
\begin{aligned}
&p_A(R_1=1\mid X_2=0,1)=(1/2,1/2),\\
&p_A(R_2=1\mid X_1=0,1,R_1=1)=(1/2,1/2),\\
&p_A(R_2=1\mid X_1=0,1,R_1=0)=(1/3,2/3),
\end{aligned}
\]
and
\[
\begin{aligned}
&p_B(R_1=1\mid X_2=0,1)=(5/9,5/11),\\
&p_B(R_2=1\mid X_1=0,1,R_1=1)=(1/2,1/2),\\
&p_B(R_2=1\mid X_1=0,1,R_1=0)=(35/54,10/27).
\end{aligned}
\]
Multiplication and summation give the common observed cells
\[
q_{11}=\begin{pmatrix}1/12&1/24\\1/24&1/12\end{pmatrix},\quad
q_{10}=(1/8,1/8),\quad q_{01}=(1/9,5/36),\quad q_{00}=1/4.
\]
Adjoining independent fair \(X_3,R_3\) gives minimum full-cell probabilities \(1/144\) and \(1/162\), and target masses \(1/6\) and \(3/20\) at \((0,0,0)\). Relabelling and ignoring additional parents therefore cover all \(654\) graphs.

The direct-association compiler itself has a denominator-safe closed form. Put \(A_i=\operatorname{pa}^X_G(i)\) and \(P_i=\operatorname{pa}^R_G(i)\). On its branch, \(i\notin A_i\) and no \(R_j\), \(j\in A_i\), is a response descendant of \(R_i\). Define the observable event
\[
B_i(x_{A_i})=\{X_{A_i}^*=x_{A_i},\ R_{A_i}=\mathbf1,\ R_{P_i}=\mathbf1\}.
\]
The local Markov property obtained from Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}graph\text{-}factorization}\) permits the nonparent, nondescendant selectors \(R_{A_i\setminus P_i}\) to be added to the conditioning set. Therefore
\[
\lambda_{i,p}(1\mid x_{A_i},\mathbf1_{P_i})
=\Pr_p\{R_i=1\mid B_i(x_{A_i})\}
=\frac{q\{B_i(x_{A_i}),R_i=1\}}{q\{B_i(x_{A_i})\}}.
\]
Both events are nonempty and have positive probability by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}denominator\text{-}safety}\). Evaluating Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}graph\text{-}factorization}\) at \(R=\mathbf1\) gives
\[
q\{X^*=x,R=\mathbf1\}
=p_X(x)\prod_{i=1}^3\lambda_{i,p}(1\mid x_{A_i},\mathbf1_{P_i}).
\]
Substitution identifies \(p_X(x)\). In the certificate grammar it is evaluated without dividing by a product: starting from the complete-case cell, for \(i=1,2,3\), multiply by \(q\{B_i(x_{A_i})\}\) and then divide by \(q\{B_i(x_{A_i}),R_i=1\}\). Thus every quotient divisor is one positive observed-event marginal. This graph-factorization and conditional-independence trace applies to each direct-association mask.

The remaining mask counts are exact. Absence of a colluder forbids one substantive arrow for each response arrow, so the number of no-self-censoring, no-colluder masks is
\[
1\cdot2^6+6\cdot2^5+12\cdot2^4+6\cdot2^3=496.
\]
Across the \(25\) response DAGs, the direct-association criterion leaves respectively \(6,5,4,3\) allowed substantive arrows with multiplicities \(1,6,6,12\), and therefore covers
\[
2^6+6\cdot2^5+6\cdot2^4+12\cdot2^3=448
\]
masks. Its intersections with the no-colluder branch total
\[
2^6+6\cdot2^4+6\cdot2^2+6\cdot2+6=202,
\]
so the ordered direct branch adds \(448-202=246\). The disjoint residual count is \(1600-654-496-246=204\). No nonidentity simultaneous item permutation fixes a residual mask, so Burnside's formula gives \(204/6=34\) residual classes.

The directive's target-level normalization step is also proved. For any positive unnormalized response weight \(a_r(x)\) satisfying
\[
p(r\mid x)=\frac{a_r(x)}{Z(x)},\qquad Z(x)=\sum_{s\in\mathcal B}a_s(x),
\]
write \(\mathbf 1=(1,1,1)\). The complete-case observed cell obeys
\[
q\{X^*=x,R=\mathbf1\}=p_X(x)\frac{a_{\mathbf1}(x)}{Z(x)}.
\]
Consequently
\[
q\{X^*=x,R=\mathbf1\}
\sum_{r\in\mathcal B}\frac{a_r(x)}{a_{\mathbf1}(x)}
=p_X(x)\frac{a_{\mathbf1}(x)}{Z(x)}
\frac{\sum_r a_r(x)}{a_{\mathbf1}(x)}
=p_X(x).
\]
Thus the \(1/Z(x)\) appearing in the Nabi--Bhattacharya--Shpitser full-law intermediate cancels identically after target projection; no division by a sum is needed. Moreover, once an elementary conditional or odds-ratio factor is written as a product of ratios \(q(A)/q(B)\), inversion of a product can be implemented by successive divisions, every divisor remains a single observed marginal \(q(A)\), and the outer sum over \(r\) is never placed in a denominator. Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}denominator\text{-}safety}\) makes every such nonempty-event divisor positive.

What remains unproved is the lower-level statement needed by the theorem: for each of the \(496\) masks, every conditional and odds-ratio factor in the inherited unnormalized weight must be derived from graph factorization, expanded into specified nonempty observed events, and emitted with an exact checker transcript and operation count. The frozen definitions name that compiler but provide neither the mask-indexed weights nor the \(496\) traces. Therefore the cancellation above cannot by itself establish that \(\operatorname{Known}_3\) returns accepted \(\mathcal L_3\) certificates on all \(496\) masks.

snapshot.stmt: The deterministic procedure \(\operatorname{Known}_3\) returns accepted rational \(\mathrm{NONID}\) certificates for \(11200\) graphs containing a self-censoring arrow and for \(654\) additional no-self-censoring graphs containing a criss-cross obstruction; it returns accepted rational \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificates for \(496\) no-self-censoring/no-colluder graphs and for \(246\) additional direct-association graphs. Exactly \(204\) labelled graphs, forming \(34\) classes in \(\mathfrak R_{34}\), remain unresolved.

defs.def:known-branches: \(\operatorname{Known}_3(G)\) applies, in order, the self-censoring twin compiler, the positive criss-cross twin compiler, the no-self-censoring/no-colluder full-law formula compiler, and the direct-association propensity compiler; it returns the first accepted \(\mathcal L_3\) certificate and otherwise returns \(\mathrm{unresolved}\).

prop:published-odds-regression.proof_tex:
Write the three positive response kernels supplied by Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}graph\text{-}factorization}\) on \(G_{\mathrm{OR}}\) as
\[
\alpha_{z,s}(r_1)=p(r_1\mid X_3=z,R_2=s),\qquad
\beta_{u,t}(r_2)=p(r_2\mid X_1=u,R_3=t),\qquad
\gamma_u(r_3)=p(r_3\mid X_1=u),
\]
and put
\[
J_{st}(u)=\beta_{u,t}(s)\gamma_u(t)
=p(R_2=s,R_3=t\mid X_1=u).
\]
Every displayed factor is strictly positive because the full joint law is strictly positive.

For \(z,s\in\{0,1\}\), summing the factorization over the unshown substantive coordinates and over \(R_1\) where appropriate gives
\[
q(R_1=1,X_3^*=z,R_3=1,R_2=s)
=\alpha_{z,s}(1)\,q(X_3^*=z,R_3=1,R_2=s).
\]
The conditioning denominator is positive by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}denominator\text{-}safety}\), so
\[
a(z,s)=\alpha_{z,s}(1).
\]
Next define the positive quantity
\[
m_s(u)=\sum_{x_2,x_3}p_X(u,x_2,x_3)\alpha_{x_3,s}(1).
\]
Direct summation of the factorization gives, for \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
p(X_1=u,R_1=1,R_2=s,R_3=t)=m_s(u)J_{st}(u).
\]
Consequently
\[
c_s(u)=\frac{J_{s1}(u)}{J_{s0}(u)+J_{s1}(u)}.
\]

Let \(h(u)=\sum_{x_2}p_X(u,x_2,0)>0\).  The two observed reference-slice masses in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}odds\text{-}functional}\) are
\[
\begin{aligned}
q(X_1^*=u,X_3^*=0,R=(1,0,1))&=h(u)\alpha_{0,0}(1)J_{01}(u),\\
q(X_1^*=u,X_3^*=0,R=(1,1,1))&=h(u)\alpha_{0,1}(1)J_{11}(u).
\end{aligned}
\]
Using \(a(0,s)=\alpha_{0,s}(1)\), all positive factors cancel exactly and yield
\[
t(u)=\frac{J_{01}(u)}{J_{11}(u)}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{c_1(u)}+\frac{t(u)}{c_0(u)}
&=\frac{J_{10}(u)+J_{11}(u)}{J_{11}(u)}
 +\frac{J_{01}(u)}{J_{11}(u)}
   \frac{J_{00}(u)+J_{01}(u)}{J_{01}(u)}\\
&=\frac{\sum_{s,t\in\{0,1\}}J_{st}(u)}{J_{11}(u)}
=\frac{1}{J_{11}(u)}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Finally, the complete-case cell satisfies
\[
q(X^*=x,R=\mathbf 1)
=p_X(x)\alpha_{x_3,1}(1)J_{11}(x_1)
=p_X(x)a(x_3,1)J_{11}(x_1).
\]
Substitution into Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}odds\text{-}functional}\) proves
\[
F_{\mathrm{OR}}(C_{\#}p)(x)=p_X(x)
\qquad(x\in\mathcal B).
\]
Each conditional probability just used is a ratio of two observed event marginals.  Expanding \(a\), \(c_s\), and \(t\) therefore expresses the calculation using only sums, products, and divisions by nonempty observed-event probabilities; all are positive by the denominator lemma.  The displayed factorization and cancellation form a finite odds-ratio trace, so Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}certificate\text{-}checker}\) accepts its encoding.  The remaining algorithmic comparison is exactly the cited Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}guo\text{-}nabi\text{-}odds\text{-}tree\text{-}failure}\).

snapshot.stmt: For every \(p\in\mathcal M_+(G_{\mathrm{OR}})\), the Scenario 1 odds-ratio identification of Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020) specializes to \[p_X(x)=F_{\mathrm{OR}}(C_{\#}p)(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal B.\] Its encoding is accepted by \(\operatorname{Check}_3\), every divisor is positive by Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}denominator\text{-}safety}\), and the intervention-tree workflow has no successful target-law trace on \(G_{\mathrm{OR}}\), as documented by Guo and Nabi (2026).

oeq:residual-dichotomy.proof_tex:
For residual case \(6\), on the positive stratum where the observed \(2\times2\) matrix \(M\) in the prior partial progress has determinant \(\Delta\neq0\), the equations \(Md=h\) give \(d=M^{-1}h\); then \(k_z=e_z/\sum_uH_{uz}d_uc_{u1}\), and
\[
p(X_1=u,X_3=z)=H_{uz}(1+k_z).
\]
The displayed denominator equals a positive graph-factorized mass and is therefore positive. Multiplication by the observed complete-case conditional law of \(X_2\) given \((X_1,X_3)\) recovers all eight target cells. The exceptional positive stratum \(\Delta=0\) is unresolved: the two aggregate equations have rank at most one, and neither the remaining \(X_2\)-specific equations nor the \(R_3=0\) equations have been shown to select a unique rational \(k_z\) or to admit rational positive twins. No accepted rows are available for the other \(33\) canonical representatives, so the required \(34\)-row ledger and exceptional-stratum audit are not established.

snapshot.stmt: Using \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{res}}\), construct the ordered canonical list \(\mathcal K_{34}\) and fill every row of \(\mathcal D_{34}\). For each of its exactly \(34\) graph rows and every positive rank or divisor stratum, supply either an accepted \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificate containing eight rational observed-law expressions with only universally positive observed-marginal divisors, or an accepted \(\mathrm{NONID}\) certificate containing two explicit strictly positive rational \(64\)-cell graph-Markov laws with equal \(27\)-cell coarsenings and different target mass at a named cell. Run \(\operatorname{AlgTest}_3\) on every exceptional stratum and establish that no uniformly identified row has output \(\mathrm{proper\ algebraic\ extension}\); certify exact row coverage, checker acceptance, and operation count in the ledger.

defs.def:algebraic-inverse-test: For each \(G^{(k)}\in\mathcal K_{34}\), express the graph factorization and the \(27\) coarsening equations as a polynomial ideal over \(\mathbb Q\), localize at the product of the \(64\) full-cell coordinates and the \(27\) observed-cell coordinates, and split only on the vanishing or nonvanishing of rank minors and certificate denominators encountered in the residual derivation. On each resulting stratum \(\mathcal S\), exact Groebner elimination and multiplication-matrix minimal polynomials determine whether the residue class of \(p_X(x)\) lies in \(\mathbb Q(q_w:w\in\mathcal W)\), lies in a proper finite algebraic extension, or varies within the algebraic fibre. Positivity and actual nonidentification are certified separately by the analytic \(\mathcal L_3\) formula or rational twin in the same ledger row. This is a finite graph-specific function-field calculation, not generic real quantifier elimination.
defs.def:canonical-representatives: Encode \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\) by the \(15\)-bit word listing the nine possible \(X_j\to R_i\) arrows followed by the six possible \(R_j\to R_i\) arrows in lexicographic index order. For \(K\in\mathfrak R_{34}\), let \(\operatorname{can}(K)\) be its lexicographically least relabelling, and define \(\mathcal K_{34}=(G^{(1)},\ldots,G^{(34)})\) by sorting the \(34\) values \(\operatorname{can}(K)\) lexicographically.
defs.def:residual-handle: For each \(G^{(k)}\in\mathcal K_{34}\), begin with a pattern-indexed state carrying its observed kernel and selection provenance; close the state under licensed intervention-tree steps, grouped partial-order fixing, conditional-independence substitutions, and reference-cell odds-ratio factorization. Split on every rank minor and candidate divisor encountered, apply \(\operatorname{AlgTest}_3\) on each exceptional stratum, and use exact finite response-fibre calculations to derive either a rational observed-marginal formula or a rational positive twin family that is expressed and checked analytically in \(\mathcal L_3\).
defs.def:residual-ledger: \(\mathcal D_{34}\) is an exactly \(34\)-row table indexed by \(\mathcal K_{34}\). Row \(k\) records the full \(15\)-bit edge word of \(G^{(k)}\), an exhaustive list of its positive rank and divisor strata, the value of \(\operatorname{AlgTest}_3\) for all eight target coordinates on each exceptional stratum, one analytic \(\mathcal L_3\) certificate covering every listed stratum, the exact \(\operatorname{Check}_3\) acceptance result, and the certificate operation count.

thm:complete3-iff.proof_tex:
If an accepted covering family \((\gamma_G:G\in\mathfrak G_3)\) and all of its finite operation counts were supplied, then the deterministic lookup, relabelling, and transport in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}complete3\text{-}handle}\) would terminate and one could set
\[
B=\max_{G\in\mathfrak G_3}\operatorname{cost}_3(\gamma_G)+b_{\mathrm{transport}},
\]
where \(b_{\mathrm{transport}}\) is the fixed exact cost of lookup and relabelling. Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}certificate\text{-}soundness}\) would make every \(\mathrm{ID}\) output identifying; every accepted twin would contradict \(\operatorname{UID}_X(G)=1\), giving the converse. This reduction also correctly places \(G_{\mathrm{OR}}\) inside the no-self-censoring/no-colluder subdomain and uses Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}published\text{-}odds\text{-}regression}\) for its target formula and tree failure. The missing \(34\)-row ledger and the absent numerical trace costs prevent instantiation of a numerical \(B\) and prevent the unconditional equivalence.

snapshot.stmt: Using the accepted \(34\)-row ledger \(\mathcal D_{34}\) as a load-bearing converse certificate, there is an explicit instantiation of \(\operatorname{Complete}_3\) and a numerical integer \(B\) such that, for every \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\), the procedure terminates with \(\operatorname{cost}_3(\operatorname{Complete}_3(G))\le B\), its output is accepted by \(\operatorname{Check}_3\), and \[\operatorname{Complete}_3(G)\text{ has terminal type }\mathrm{ID}\Longleftrightarrow\operatorname{UID}_X(G)=1.\] On the \(\mathrm{ID}\) branch it returns eight denominator-safe rational expressions \(F_G\); on the other branch it returns explicit strictly positive rational observational twins. The converse uses the ledger's exhaustive canonical coverage and exceptional-stratum \(\operatorname{AlgTest}_3\) outcomes, not generic real quantifier elimination. On the no-self-censoring/no-colluder subdomain the \(\mathrm{ID}\) output reduces to the target marginal of the full-law functional of Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020), while \(G_{\mathrm{OR}}\) belongs to that subdomain and is not accepted by the intervention-tree workflow.

On each resulting stratum \(\mathcal S\), exact Groebner elimination and multiplication-matrix minimal polynomials determine whether the residue class of \(p_X(x)\) lies in \(\mathbb Q(q_w:w\in\mathcal W)\), lies in a proper finite algebraic extension, or varies within the algebraic fibre. Positivity and actual nonidentification are certified separately by the analytic \(\mathcal L_3\) formula or rational twin in the same ledger row. This is a finite graph-specific function-field calculation, not generic real quantifier elimination.

For \(K\in\mathfrak R_{34}\), let \(\operatorname{can}(K)\) be its lexicographically least relabelling, and define \(\mathcal K_{34}=(G^{(1)},\ldots,G^{(34)})\) by sorting the \(34\) values \(\operatorname{can}(K)\) lexicographically.
defs.def:complete3-handle: Instantiate \(\operatorname{Complete}_3\) by running \(\operatorname{Known}_3\), applying simultaneous item relabelling and graph-inclusion transport to accepted certificates, and otherwise locating the unique canonical representative in \(\mathcal K_{34}\) and reading its accepted certificate from \(\mathcal D_{34}\); return the transported accepted \(\mathcal L_3\) certificate.

Row \(k\) records the full \(15\)-bit edge word of \(G^{(k)}\), an exhaustive list of its positive rank and divisor strata, the value of \(\operatorname{AlgTest}_3\) for all eight target coordinates on each exceptional stratum, one analytic \(\mathcal L_3\) certificate covering every listed stratum, the exact \(\operatorname{Check}_3\) acceptance result, and the certificate operation count.
defs.def:uniform-id: \[\operatorname{UID}_X(G)=1\Longleftrightarrow\left[\forall p^{(0)},p^{(1)}\in\mathcal M_+(G),\ C_{\#}p^{(0)}=C_{\#}p^{(1)}\Rightarrow\sum_r p^{(0)}(x,r)=\sum_r p^{(1)}(x,r)\text{ for every }x\in\mathcal B\right].\]

thm:strict-method-frontier.proof_tex: Conditionally on Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}complete3\text{-}iff}\), sound successful intervention-tree and grouped-fixing traces must land on the \(\mathrm{ID}\) branch. Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}published\text{-}odds\text{-}regression}\) and Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}guo\text{-}nabi\text{-}odds\text{-}tree\text{-}failure}\) certify that \(G_{\mathrm{OR}}\) makes the intervention-tree inclusion strict. The frozen core supplies no result showing that \(\operatorname{GroupFix}_3\) rejects \(G_{\mathrm{OR}}\), or any other graph that \(\operatorname{Complete}_3\) identifies. It also supplies no completed \(496\)-mask compilation proving algebraic equality of every returned no-colluder target formula with the published full-law marginal. Hence the two-method strictness and subdomain-equality clauses remain open.

snapshot.stmt: For every \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\), a successful \(\operatorname{Tree}_3(G)\) trace or \(\operatorname{GroupFix}_3(G)\) trace transports to an \(\mathrm{ID}\) certificate returned by \(\operatorname{Complete}_3(G)\). Both acceptance-set inclusions are strict: \(G_{\mathrm{OR}}\) is classified \(\mathrm{ID}\) through the published functional \(F_{\mathrm{OR}}\) and is not accepted by either fixing search. On every graph with no self-censoring arrow and no colluder, the returned target functional is algebraically equal to the target marginal of the full-law odds-ratio functional of Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020).

defs.def:certificate-language: \(\mathcal L_3\) has two terminal forms. An \(\mathrm{ID}\) term contains eight expressions formed from the coordinates of \(q\) by finite sums, products, and quotients; every quotient denominator is encoded as \(q(A)=\sum_{w\in A}q_w\) for a checker-certified nonempty event \(A\subseteq\mathcal W\). Its trace uses graph factorization, conditional independence, grouped fixing, intervention fixing, or Chen odds-ratio identities, and each constructor records all input and output divisors. A \(\mathrm{NONID}\) term contains two rational \(64\)-cell tables, their graph-factorized conditional tables, exact equality of their \(27\) coarsened cells, strict-positivity checks, and a named cell where their target marginals differ.

thm:compiled-inference.proof_tex:
Fix \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\) for which \(\operatorname{Complete}_3(G)\) has terminal type \(\mathrm{ID}\), and fix \(\epsilon\in(0,1/64)\). Let \(p\in\mathcal M_\epsilon(G)\) and put \(q=C_\#p\). Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}complete3\text{-}iff}\) says that the returned certificate is accepted by \(\operatorname{Check}_3\); Theorem \(\mathrm{thm{:}certificate\text{-}soundness}\) therefore gives
\[
F_G(q)=p_X.
\]
For each \(w\in\mathcal W\), the fibre \(C^{-1}\{w\}\) is nonempty. Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}law}\) and Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\text{-}interior}\) consequently imply
\[
q_w=\sum_{(x,r):C(x,r)=w}p(x,r)\geq\epsilon.
\]
Thus every nonempty observed event \(A\subseteq\mathcal W\) satisfies \(q(A)\geq\epsilon\). By Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}certificate\text{-}denominator\text{-}safety}\), these are exactly the possible divisors in the fixed rational expression \(F_G\).

Let
\[
K_{G,\epsilon}=\{C_\#p:p\in\mathcal M_\epsilon(G)\}.
\]
This set is compact. Indeed, the inequalities \(p(x,r)\geq\epsilon\) define a compact subset of the finite probability simplex. On this subset all conditional probabilities occurring in Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}graph\text{-}factorization}\) have positive marginal denominators and hence are continuous functions of \(p\); the factorization equalities therefore define a closed subset, namely \(\mathcal M_\epsilon(G)\). The linear map \(C_\#\) is continuous, proving compactness of \(K_{G,\epsilon}\).

Because \(F_G\) is a finite rational expression and each of its divisors is at least \(\epsilon\) on \(K_{G,\epsilon}\), there is an open neighborhood of this compact set on which \(F_G\) is twice continuously differentiable. Its second derivative has there a finite uniform operator-norm bound, denoted by \(M_{G,\epsilon}\). Write \(\delta_n=\widehat q-q\), and let \(E_n\) be the event that every empirical divisor required by \(F_G\) is positive. If the certificate uses \(d_G<\infty\) distinct divisor events, then independence in Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid\text{-}coarsened\text{-}sampling}\) and the lower bound above give
\[
\sup_{p\in\mathcal M_\epsilon(G)}\Pr_p(E_n^c)
\leq \sum_{A\ {\rm required}}\{1-q(A)\}^n
\leq d_G(1-\epsilon)^n
\leq d_G e^{-n\epsilon}.
\]
Hence the pseudocount branch in Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}plugin\text{-}estimator}\) is used with uniformly vanishing probability.

Put \(D_n=\{\lVert\delta_n\rVert_1\leq\epsilon/2\}\). The exact multinomial second moment is
\[
\mathbb E_q\lVert\widehat q-q\rVert_2^2
=\frac{\operatorname{tr}\{\operatorname{diag}(q)-qq^{\mathsf T}\}}{n}
=\frac{1-\lVert q\rVert_2^2}{n}\leq\frac1n.
\]
Since \(\lVert v\rVert_1^2\leq27\lVert v\rVert_2^2\), the elementary inequality \(\Pr(Y>a)\leq\mathbb E(Y)/a\) for \(Y\geq0\) yields
\[
\sup_{p\in\mathcal M_\epsilon(G)}\Pr_p(D_n^c)
\leq\frac{108}{n\epsilon^2}.
\]
On \(D_n\), every required divisor on the segment \(q+t\delta_n\), \(0\leq t\leq1\), is at least \(\epsilon/2\). Taylor's formula with integral remainder gives
\[
F_G(\widehat q)-F_G(q)=D F_G(q)\delta_n+R_n,
\qquad
R_n=\int_0^1\{D F_G(q+t\delta_n)-D F_G(q)\}\delta_n\,dt,
\]
and therefore
\[
\lVert R_n\rVert_2\leq\frac{M_{G,\epsilon}}2\lVert\delta_n\rVert_2^2
\quad\hbox{on }D_n.
\]
For every \(\eta>0\), the same nonnegative-variable inequality and the preceding moment identity imply
\[
\sup_{p\in\mathcal M_\epsilon(G)}
\Pr_p\{\sqrt n\lVert R_n\rVert_2>\eta,\ D_n\}
\leq\frac{M_{G,\epsilon}}{2\eta\sqrt n}.
\]
Together with the bounds for \(D_n^c\) and \(E_n^c\), this proves \(\sqrt nR_n=o_p(1)\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_\epsilon(G)\). Since
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat q-q)=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{j=1}^n(e_{W_j}-q),
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}compiled\text{-}influence}\) now gives
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat p_X-p_X)
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{j=1}^n\varphi_G(W_j;q)+o_p(1).
\]

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}finite\text{-}multinomial\text{-}clt}\) gives the multinomial Gaussian limit for every fixed \(q\). Here its characteristic-function calculation is uniform in \(q\). Indeed, for every fixed \(t\in\mathbb R^{27}\), boundedness of \(e_W-q\) and the third-order Taylor formula give
\[
\mathbb E_q\exp\!\left\{\frac{i t^{\mathsf T}(e_W-q)}{\sqrt n}\right\}
=1-\frac{t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(q)t}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}),
\]
where the remainder constant depends on \(t\) but not on \(q\). Raising this expression to the \(n\)-th power gives, uniformly for \(q\in K_{G,\epsilon}\),
\[
\exp\{-t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma(q)t/2\}+o(1).
\]
The same calculation after applying the uniformly bounded linear map \(D F_G(q)\) proves
\[
\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{j=1}^n\varphi_G(W_j;q)
\rightsquigarrow N_8(0,V_G(q))
\]
uniformly in bounded-Lipschitz distance. This argument never inverts \(V_G(q)\), so singularity is allowed.

The map
\[
q\longmapsto D F_G(q)\{\operatorname{diag}(q)-qq^{\mathsf T}\}D F_G(q)^{\mathsf T}
\]
is uniformly continuous on a neighborhood of \(K_{G,\epsilon}\). The displayed second-moment identity gives \(\widehat q-q=o_p(1)\) uniformly, and the pseudocount event is negligible. Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}compiled\text{-}influence}\) and the plug-in formula for \(\widehat V_G\) therefore imply
\[
\widehat V_G\longrightarrow_p V_G(q)
\]
uniformly over \(p\in\mathcal M_\epsilon(G)\).

It remains to justify studentization without assuming that the eight-dimensional covariance is nonsingular. Fix \(x\in\mathcal B\), write \(g_x=D F_G(q)(x,\cdot)\), and suppose that \(V_G(q)(x,x)=0\). Since every \(q_w>0\),
\[
0=g_x\Sigma(q)g_x^{\mathsf T}=\operatorname{Var}_q\{g_x(W)\}
\]
forces \(g_x(w)\) to be constant in \(w\). Choose \(y\in\mathcal B\setminus\{x\}\). Keep all response kernels of \(p\) fixed and, for sufficiently small \(|t|\), replace the target law by
\[
p_{X,t}=p_X+t(\mathbf 1_{\{x\}}-\mathbf 1_{\{y\}}).
\]
Strict positivity of \(p\), which follows from Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}fixed\text{-}interior}\), ensures that the resulting factorized law \(p_t\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_+(G)\). If \(q_t=C_\#p_t\), certificate soundness gives \(F_G(q_t)(x)=p_X(x)+t\). Differentiating at zero yields
\[
1=g_x\left.\frac{d q_t}{dt}\right|_{t=0}.
\]
But \(\sum_w d q_t(w)/dt=0\), so a constant \(g_x\) makes the right-hand side zero, a contradiction. Hence \(V_G(q)(x,x)>0\) for every \(q\in K_{G,\epsilon}\) and \(x\in\mathcal B\). Continuity, compactness, and finiteness of \(\mathcal B\) give
\[
\nu_{G,\epsilon}:=\min_{q\in K_{G,\epsilon}}\min_{x\in\mathcal B}V_G(q)(x,x)>0.
\]
Thus the eight coordinatewise studentized statistics converge uniformly to standard normal variables, although their joint covariance may be singular.

Let \(z=z_{1-\alpha/16}\). Each two-sided coordinate error then has limiting probability at most \(2\{1-\Phi(z)\}=\alpha/8\), uniformly in \(p\). Since \(p_X\in\Delta_7\), Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}simultaneous\text{-}region}\) and the union bound give
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{p\in\mathcal M_\epsilon(G)}
\Pr_p\{p_X\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(G)\}
\geq1-8\frac{\alpha}{8}=1-\alpha.
\]
This proves every assertion.

snapshot.stmt: Fix \(G\in\mathfrak G_3\) with an \(\mathrm{ID}\) output and \(\epsilon\in(0,1/64)\). Uniformly over \(p\in\mathcal M_{\epsilon}(G)\), \[\sqrt n\{\widehat p_X-p_X\}=\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\varphi_G(W_j;q)+o_p(1)\rightsquigarrow N_8(0,V_G(q)),\] where \(V_G(q)\) may be singular, \(\widehat V_G\to_p V_G(q)\), and \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{p\in\mathcal M_{\epsilon}(G)}\Pr_p\{p_X\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(G)\}\ge1-\alpha.\]

defs.def:plugin-estimator: \[\widehat p_X=F_G(\widehat q),\qquad \widehat q_w=\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^{n}\mathbf 1\{W_j=w\},\] with a fixed unit pseudocount in all \(27\) cells only on samples where a required empirical divisor is zero.
defs.def:simultaneous-region: \[\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}(G)=\left\{v\in\Delta_7:|v_x-\widehat p_X(x)|\le z_{1-\alpha/16}\sqrt{\widehat V_G(x,x)/n}\text{ for all }x\in\mathcal B\right\}.\]

prose_overlay.tldr: For binary three-item conditional-MNAR DAGs, exact enumeration and explicit positive rational witnesses establish the conservative reduction to 204 labelled graphs in 34 relabelling classes. The no-self-censoring/no-colluder full-law construction contains a normalizing factor \(1/Z(x)\), but target projection cancels it universally: \(p_X(x)=q\{X^*=x,R=\mathbf1\}\sum_r a_r(x)/a_{\mathbf1}(x)\). What remains open in that 496-graph branch is the lower-level audit that expands every identified conditional and odds-ratio interaction into the restrictive raw observed-marginal certificate grammar and records checker acceptance and operation counts. The 34-class residual dichotomy, the total Complete3 equivalence, the grouped-fixing strictness claim, and the numerical operation bound also remain open. Conditional on any accepted ID formula, the fixed-interior multinomial influence function, covariance estimator, and simultaneous confidence region are proved.
prose_overlay.related_work: Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (2020, Theorems 1--2, Scenario 1, and Conclusion) establish the no-self-censoring/no-colluder full-law frontier and use a normalized odds-ratio factorization. For the target marginal, the normalizing \(1/Z(x)\) cancels algebraically, but their paper does not supply the present 496-mask compilation into a certificate grammar whose every divisor is a raw positive observed-event marginal. Bhattacharya, Nabi, Shpitser, and Robins (2020, Proposition 1, Lemma 2, and Section 6) introduce grouped partial-order fixing but do not provide a complete search or a documented false negative matching the claimed strict frontier. Guo and Nabi (2026, Algorithm 1, Theorem 1, Figure E.2(a), and Section 8) provide a sound intervention-tree workflow and document the odds-ratio graph as a false negative, which certifies strictness only for that comparator. Tikka and Karvanen (2024) address categorical colluders under rank conditions rather than every positive rank-degenerate law. Duarte et al. (2023) provide generic polynomial optimization, not graph-specific rational formulas or positive rational twins. The multinomial inference layer is a finite-dimensional consequence of an accepted rational certificate and is not claimed as the novelty kernel.
prose_overlay.technical_internal_limitation: A rational polynomial parameterization alone does not imply the required rational certificate dichotomy: an injective observation map may have only a non-rational algebraic inverse, and a nonidentifying exact fibre may contain no distinct rational points. The 34 residual rows therefore still require explicit exceptional-stratum analysis. Separately, cancellation of the Nabi--Bhattacharya--Shpitser normalizer proves only \(q\{X^*=x,R=\mathbf1\}\sum_r a_r(x)/a_{\mathbf1}(x)=p_X(x)\); it does not prove that every mask-specific factor \(a_r/a_{\mathbf1}\) has already been compiled into allowed \(q(A)\) leaves. No 496-row compiler output, checker transcript, or operation-count ledger is present in the frozen core.
prose_overlay.honest_scope: Exact rational calculations verify the self-censoring and criss-cross twins, the graph counts, the 204/34 conservative residual reduction, the direct-association target formula, and the universal cancellation of the full-law odds-ratio normalizer. They do not establish the theorem's assertion that all 496 no-self-censoring/no-colluder masks already have accepted raw-observed-marginal certificates. Residual case 6 is solved only on \(\Delta\ne0\); its positive rank-degenerate stratum and the other residual rows remain open. Consequently the Complete3 iff theorem, a numerical \(B\), and grouped-fixing strictness are not yet proved. The compiled inference theorem is established conditionally on a checker-accepted ID output. The model remains binary with three items, assumes full joint support and a supplied graph, excludes latent variables and response-to-substantive arrows, and makes no boundary, graph-learning, continuous-variable, or unpublished-result claim.

project_justification.gap: Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser give a complete criterion and an odds-ratio construction for the full law but do not provide the requested graph-uniform target-law classifier or a 496-mask compilation into raw observed-marginal denominators. Grouped fixing and intervention trees are constructive sufficient procedures; only the intervention-tree false negative is certified in the present core. Rank-based colluder results do not settle positive rank-degenerate strata.
project_justification.niche: With exactly three binary items, the graph universe and the coarsened law are finite, and explicit obstruction witnesses already reduce the problem to 34 relabelling classes. The remaining issue is not the global normalizer in the published full-law formula, because target projection cancels it, but the local graph-by-graph rational expansion and the exceptional positive fibres.
project_justification.fill: The established part supplies exact graph counts, explicit positive rational self-censoring and criss-cross twins, a denominator-safe direct-association compiler, the universal target-level cancellation of the full-law normalizer, and fixed-interior inference for any accepted rational formula. Completion still requires the 496-mask raw-marginal compiler audit, the 34-row residual ledger, an actual numerical trace bound, and a grouped-fixing false-negative certificate if two-method strictness is retained.

sampling_model.overlap: The classification model has full joint support. Under the frozen grammar this makes every nonempty observed-event marginal positive; under the proposed extension it also makes every recursively certified subtraction-free divisor positive. For uniform inference, the fixed class \(\mathcal M_{\epsilon}(G)\) supplies compactness and uniform lower bounds for every divisor in any fixed accepted trace.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional on a checker-accepted ID certificate, no infinite-dimensional nuisance is estimated: \(F_G\), its derivative, and \(V_G\) are evaluated at the empirical 27-cell multinomial vector, with the fixed unit pseudocount used only on the exponentially rare event that a required empirical divisor vanishes.

thm:certified-reduction.justification: This theorem is the conservative finite reduction, but its accepted-certificate formulation additionally requires a lower-level compiler receipt rather than only the published full-law identification theorem.
thm:certified-reduction.gap: The exact counts, twin constructions, direct-association formulas, and target-level normalizer cancellation are established. The missing proof is the 496-mask raw-observed-marginal expansion, exact checker transcript, and operation-count audit.
thm:certified-reduction.consumer: Once the 496 traces are supplied, Known3 can expose executable denominator-safe formulas for that branch and leave exactly the 34 canonical residual cases to the ledger stage.

thm:compiled-inference.justification: For every checker-accepted rational ID formula, the theorem now supplies a uniform asymptotic linear expansion, a consistent possibly singular covariance estimator, and simultaneous coordinate coverage on the fixed interior subclass.
thm:compiled-inference.gap: This inference theorem is conditional on an accepted ID output and does not discharge any missing identification or certificate-compilation step.
thm:compiled-inference.consumer: flexMissing can attach joint uncertainty quantification immediately to every ID certificate once that certificate is available.

prose_overlay.interpretation: The target-level cancellation shows that the published full-law normalizer is not itself an obstruction to the requested certificate language: sums remain outside denominators, and inverses of products can be evaluated by successive divisions. The unresolved risk is local. Every one of the 496 graph masks still needs its identified conditional and odds-ratio factors expressed as ratios of explicitly encoded nonempty observed events, with the algebraic trace checked exactly.
